title: Payment connection pool timeouts
executive_summary: payment-service's DB connection pool (payment-db-pool) was cut from max_size 50 to 10 by a config change at 10:04Z (cfg-56d39584, config-bot, OPS-2669). Pool utilisation hit 100% from 10:05-10:10, and the pool timeout errors began at 10:06, with error rate rising from ~0.8% to ~17% and timeouts from ~0.1% to ~12%. The pool-exhaustion symptom is therefore consistent with the config change, and it precedes the errors. It does not look like last year's connection leak: Postgres connection utilisation dropped rather than rose. The reported latency increase is not visible in the p99 metric (flat at ~300ms), so the impact is errors/timeouts rather than latency.

hypotheses.description: Config change reduced db.pool.max_size from 50 to 10 at 10:04Z, starving the payment DB pool under normal load. Mechanism: With max_size=10, active connections saturate at 10 with idle=0 and a growing waiting queue (up to 92). Requests then time out after 5000ms waiting for a connection, producing errors and timeouts. Postgres connection use falls at the same time, consistent with fewer client connections being opened. Request rate is unchanged, so the cause is capacity, not traffic.

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): configuration_regression in payment-service - Config change reduced db.pool.max_size from 50 to 10 at 10:04Z, starving the payment DB pool under normal load.
corrective_actions: Roll back db.pool.max_size from 10 to 50 for payment-service (OPS-2669) and confirm the pool recovers
Check that the change was intentional with the OPS-2669 owner and config-bot author
Make sure the rollback restores error and timeout rates to baseline (~0.8% errors, ~0.1% timeouts)
preventive_actions: Add validation/guardrails in CI or the config service to flag large pool-size reductions (e.g. >50%) without approval
Require peer review for automated config-bot changes to database pool settings
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on db pool utilisation >80% sustained for 2+ minutes and on pool wait-queue length
Alert on payment-service timeout_rate >1% and error_rate >2%
Track config change events for db.pool.* keys as annotations on dashboards
limitations: No pool checkout/return or wait-time metrics were available
Latency p99 did not show the reported increase, so the report's latency claim is not confirmed by telemetry
No deployments were found in the window; this was checked only for payment-service, api-gateway and postgres
The tool-call budget was not exhausted; no evidence gaps arose from failed calls
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The most likely cause is the config change db.pool.max_size 50 -> 10 at 10:04Z (cfg-56d39584). It precedes the pool saturation (10:05), the timeouts (10:06) and the error spike, and no deployment or upstream change explains it. The Postgres side is not saturated and the connection count fell, which argues against last year's leak pattern. Status is PROBABLE rather than CONFIRMED because the intent behind the change is unverified and the latency symptom is not reproduced in p99 metrics. Rolling back the config and checking recovery would confirm it.
